# PART 1: THE STRATEGIC FRAME

## 1.1 The positioning rule

**Sell the emotional outcome. Prove it with the mechanism. Never lead with the mechanism.**

Owners do not want a CRM, an audit, better ads, or AI follow-up. They want predictable revenue, a team they can trust, patients who come back, and a practice that does not require them to be in the building. Everything in this document leads with the second list and proves it with the first.

The reframe in one line: **you do not have a revenue problem, you have a revenue that requires you problem.**

## 1.2 The working title

**Primary title:**
> **The $100K Month With Nothing Left: How Med Spa Owners Build Revenue That's Predictable, a Team That Sells Without Them, and a Practice They Can Actually Leave**

**Alternates to split-test:**
- Owned By Your Own Business: The 60-Minute Class for Med Spa Owners Who Can't Take a Vacation
- Where Did The Money Go? A Live Class on Profit, Payroll, and the $100K Month That Left You Broke
- The Practice That Doesn't Need You

**Why the primary wins:** it is the sentence they have said in their own head, and it names all three deliverables in the subhead. It also self-qualifies. An owner who has never had a $100K month is not the buyer.

## 1.3 The three promises of the class

Every med spa owner at this level is carrying nine pains. You cannot address nine things in an hour. Cluster them into three, and each teaching block resolves one:

| Block | Emotional pain it resolves | What they leave with |
|---|---|---|
| 1. The Money | Financial fear, decision fatigue, marketing frustration | Where the money actually went, and the three numbers that end the guessing |
| 2. The Team | Team distrust, staffing churn, being the only closer | Why nobody sells like them, and what has to change so someone does |
| 3. The Return | Retention, feeling trapped, unpredictable months | How to build revenue that shows up before the month starts |

The fourth pain cluster, fear of failure and comparison, is never taught. It is named once in the origin story and once in the bridge. Name it, do not dwell on it, and never exploit it.

## 1.4 Who this is for

Independent med spa owners doing $500K to $2M annually. Usually the top producer in their own building. Often invested savings, sometimes leveraged their home, frequently left a stable clinical career. They are not lazy, uninformed, or unmotivated. They are at capacity, and every problem in the practice routes through one person.

**Tone rule for the entire funnel:** never condescend, never imply they did it wrong, never speak to them like a student. Speak to them like a peer who has seen inside forty practices that look exactly like theirs. Their situation is structural, not personal, and every line of copy should carry that.

- **Primary:** apply for a Blueprint Call. Application-gated, limited spots.
- **Secondary:** the $29 Revenue Leak Audit with KPI Calculator, framed as "find out where your money went" rather than as a discount or a downsell.

| Show-up rate (live) | 25% | 35% | 45%+ |

| $29 audit take rate (of attendees) | 8% | 15% | 22%+ |
| Applications booked (of attendees) | 3% | 6% | 10%+ |
| Application to closed partnership | 15% | 25% | 35%+ |

At 200 registrations, a 35 percent show rate, and a 6 percent application rate, you book roughly 4 calls per event. This is a weekly or biweekly machine, not a one-time launch. Build it to repeat.

You get the KPI Calculator I use with clients and a structured audit that shows you your margin, your real cost per patient, your lifetime value, and exactly where the money's going.
>
> Twenty-nine dollars to stop guessing about your own business. I'm not going to pretend that's a serious financial decision. If you take one thing from this hour, take that.
>
> Both links are in the chat. Apply for the Blueprint Call, or grab the audit. Do one of them before you close this window.
>
> Now, Q&A. Bring me your hardest questions, and bring me your numbers.

---

# PART 6: Q&A THAT CLOSES (0:57 to end)

Q&A is your second and third close, not an epilogue. Never end because questions ran out. Seed your own if the chat is quiet.

**Answer every question in three beats:** answer honestly, tell a 20-second client story that proves it, return to the link.

**"How fast do people see results?"**
> The team training and the front desk fixes move numbers in two to three weeks, because you're converting traffic you already have. Membership and retention compound over sixty to ninety days. Acquisition is slowest, which is exactly why we don't start there. Anyone promising you thirty days on everything is selling you something.

**"I already have a marketing agency."**
> Keep them if they're good. We're not the same thing. Their job is bringing people to the door. Ours is making sure the building holds water and the team converts what walks in. If your agency's decent, our work makes their numbers look better. And after the audit you'll finally know whether they're performing, because you'll have the lifetime value number you've been evaluating them without.

**"My team won't buy in."**
> Most common real objection, and it's legitimate. Two things. First, that's why compensation design is in the build. When the change makes them money, resistance drops dramatically. Second, we do the training. It isn't you walking into a staff meeting alone with new rules. It's an outside expert setting a standard, which is a completely different dynamic and you know it is.

**"I can't afford it right now."**
> I hear you, and I want to answer it seriously instead of talking you out of it. Run one number. What's your consult close rate costing you? For most practices at your size the gap between a forty-five percent close and a sixty-five percent close is around eighty-five thousand a year. That's one leak. If that's true in your practice, the question isn't whether you can afford the partnership. It's whether you can afford another year of the leak. And if the cash genuinely isn't there this quarter, don't force it. Do the twenty-nine dollar audit, find out what the leaks are actually worth, and come back when the numbers make the decision for you.

**"Is this only for injectables?"**
> No. Any practice with consults, treatment plans, and repeat visits. Lasers, body contouring, wellness, hormones. The service mix changes the math, not the structure.

**"Why is it so expensive?"** (Ask this yourself if nobody does.)
> Fair question. Compare it to what it replaces. A director of operations who could install some of this is ninety thousand a year plus benefits. A sales trainer alone is a five-figure engagement. An agency is four to eight thousand a month and doesn't touch operations. Then compare it to the leaks. If one leak is eighty-five thousand a year, the partnership is paid for before we finish installing. The expensive option is the year where nothing changes.

**"What if it doesn't work for me?"**
> That's what the guarantee is for on the Premium tier, in writing. And it's what the Blueprint Call is for. If I don't think we can produce a return, I'll tell you on the call and I won't take your money. I'd rather have a clean no than a bad client.

## The final close

> We're at time. Two links, one more time.
>
> If you know, apply for the Blueprint Call. Three spots.
>
> If you're not there, take the twenty-nine dollar audit. Everyone should do that one.
>
> And if you do neither, please do this. This week, run your operating margin, your real cost per patient, and your close rate. Write those three numbers down. You've been running this practice on feel and it's been costing you sleep. You deserve to know what's actually true.
>
> Thank you for an hour of your time. It's the most expensive thing you own, and I know exactly what it cost you to sit still for it. Go find your money.

---

# PART 7: POST-EVENT EMAIL CADENCE

Built on Ashley's post-event cadence structure, rewritten for emotional positioning. Segment on day two: audit buyers, attendee non-buyers, no-shows.

| Day | Segment | Subject | Content |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0, within 2 hours | Attendees | Your links, and the three numbers | Replay 48 hours, both CTAs, the three numbers to run tonight. Short. |
| 0 | No-shows | You missed it, so here's the big one | Deliver the margin and money block in full. Replay 24 hours only. Both links. |
| 1 | Non-buyers | Where the money actually went | Full margin and acquisition cost teardown. Ends on the $29 audit. |
| 2 | Non-buyers | Nobody sells like you. Here's why. | The three teachable differences. Ends on the Blueprint Call. |
| 3 | Non-buyers | The month that starts at zero | Retention and membership. The freedom outcome, told through a client story. |
| 4 | Non-buyers | 50 clients in 90 days, in writing | The guarantee explained including the contingencies. Transparency about contingencies raises belief rather than lowering it. |
| 5 | Non-buyers | "I can't afford it right now" | The three real objections answered directly. Price, timing, team buy-in. |
| 6 | Non-buyers | Replay comes down tonight | Final urgency, both links, spots remaining. |
| 7 | Audit buyers | Your audit, and what it means | Delivery plus the natural upgrade to a Blueprint Call. Your warmest segment. |
| 10 | All non-buyers | The capacity ceiling | Pure value, no ask beyond a soft link. Rebuilds goodwill for the next event. |
| 14 | All non-buyers | Come to the next one | Roll them into the next cohort. Never let a registrant list go cold. |

Two rules. Every email delivers something usable even if they never buy, because the list is a long-term asset. And the audit buyers get a phone call, not just an email. They paid you money and self-identified.

---

# PART 8: TECH, TEAM, AND PRE-FLIGHT

## Stack
- **Platform:** Zoom Webinar or StreamYard to a custom page. Nothing attendees have to install.
- **Registration and follow-up:** GHL, with revenue range mapped to a segmentation tag from day one.
- **Slides:** 30 to 40. One number or one sentence per slide. The margin and close-rate math should build one line at a time.
- **Chat moderator:** Aanchal or a team member live in chat the whole hour, dropping links on cue, handling logistics, flagging buying signals and good questions. Routinely skipped, worth real money.

## Pre-flight checklist
1. Run the full script out loud with a timer, twice.
2. Pull three real anonymized client examples with actual dollar figures for Block 1. Specificity is the entire game. Generic benchmarks land soft.
3. Have both links pre-written in a text file for instant pasting.
4. Test the application form and the $29 checkout on your own phone.
5. Decide the real number of spots before going live and never say a number you won't honor.
6. Set the replay window and enforce it.
7. Record everything. The first three runs are rehearsal for the evergreen version.

## After three live runs
Cut the highest-converting recording into an evergreen replay funnel and run cold traffic continuously. Keep one live event monthly for fresh material and testimonials. Live is where the offer gets sharpened. Evergreen is where it scales.

You're right, and it broke more than the ads. Course fatigue was the spine of the whole thing, so I rebuilt it rather than swapped headlines.

**The new spine:** revenue that requires you isn't an asset, it's a job with extra risk. Two practices at $1.5M, one where the owner produces 60% and closes everything herself, one where the team closes and 35% recurs monthly. Identical top line, completely different lives. One is sellable, one is unsellable because what a buyer would be purchasing is her.

**Nine pains clustered into three teaching blocks,** because you can't resolve nine in an hour:

- **The Money** (financial fear, agency frustration, decision fatigue): revenue and money aren't the same thing, operating margin, service mix, real cost per patient. The agency frustration gets explained, not just validated: they were evaluating agencies without ever knowing lifetime value, so they were arguing about a guess.
- **The Team** (distrust, staffing, being the only closer): validates that nobody sells like her, then challenges it. It's not a talent gap, it's three teachable things. And the reframe on turnover: stop trying to make people stay, build a practice where their leaving is survivable.
- **The Return** (retention, trapped, unpredictable months): the real anxiety isn't the number, it's the reset on the first of every month.

**Fear of failure gets named once,** in the origin story, then never touched again. "You put your savings in this. Some of you put your house in. What happens if this doesn't work, after everybody believed in me." Followed immediately by permission: you're a clinician who was never handed a business operating system. That's structural, not personal. Dwelling on that pain would be manipulative, and this audience would feel it.

The five ads now run financial fear, trapped, team, retention, and a video on comparison. Ad one is the $100K month that left them broke.

One thing I'd push on: the $29 audit is now the strongest CTA in the deck, because financial fear is the loudest pain and the audit answers it directly. Consider making it more prominent than three partnership spots.
